title: Cinema on Saturday
intro: Deniz ile Emma'nın sinema planı yaptığı mesajlaşmayı okuyacaksın.
text:
Deniz: Hi Emma! What are you doing on Saturday?
Emma: Nothing special. I am at home. Why?
Deniz: There is a new film at the Star Cinema. It is a comedy.
Emma: Nice! What time does it start?
Deniz: At seven o'clock. But the tickets are cheap before six.

I get up at half past six. I am always tired, but I open the window and drink a big glass of water.
At seven o'clock I have breakfast with my sister Elif. She makes tea.
I walk to school. It is twenty minutes.
Lessons start at eight. My favourite lesson is science, because our teacher is funny.

In the evening I help my mother in the kitchen. Then I watch a film.
I go to bed at eleven. Tomorrow is Wednesday and I have got a maths exam!

Deniz

MY LIFE IN THREE CITIES
Posted by Elif Kaya · March 14

Hello! I have had this blog for two years now, but I have never told you my own story. So here it is.

I grew up in Izmir. My father was a fisherman, and I used to help him on the boat every summer. I hated it when I was ten. Now I miss it.

When I was nineteen, I moved to Ankara to study engineering. I was terrible at it. One evening, while I was studying for an exam, I started drawing small houses in my notebook. My teacher saw them and said, "You should study design."

I have lived in Istanbul since 2019. I work for a small studio near Kadıköy, and I have already designed four cafés. It is harder than engineering, but it is much more fun.

Next year I am going to open my own studio. I am a little afraid, but my father always says the same thing: "A fisherman must not wait for good weather." He is right.

Have you ever changed your job? Tell me below!

RIVERTON DAILY — Local News

Old Mill Bridge Opens Again
By Clara Novak, 12 May

The Old Mill Bridge opened again on Saturday morning after six months of repair work. More than three hundred people came to the small park next to the river at nine o'clock.

The mayor, Deniz Yalın, cut the red ribbon. "This bridge is safer and wider than the old one," she said. "Children can walk to school here now."

The bridge closed last November because heavy rain damaged the stone under it. While the workers were fixing it, people used the bus or drove ten kilometres to the next bridge. Many shops near the river lost money.

"I have lived here for thirty years, and I have never seen the bridge closed before," said Mr Owens, who sells bread on Green Street. "My customers are already coming back."

The town spent 1.2 million euros on the project. The council will plant fifty new trees along the river path next spring. Visitors should use the free car park behind the library.

title: do or does?
intro: Alışkanlıkları anlatırken fiilin ne zaman -s aldığını ve soruda do/does'ın nasıl çalıştığını öğren.
focus: Present simple: do / does ve üçüncü tekilde -s

explanation.heading: Ne zaman kullanılır?
explanation.tr: Alışkanlık, rutin ve genel doğrular için: her sabah kahve içmek, bir şehirde yaşamak. Türkçede -r/-ir eki ne yapıyorsa (içerim, yaşarım) present simple onu yapar.

examples.de: I drink coffee every morning.
She lives in Berlin.
They work at a bank.

explanation.heading: Üçüncü tekilde -s
explanation.tr: he / she / it ile fiil -s alır: work → works, live → lives. Sonu -o, -sh, -ch ile bitenlerde -es: goes, watches. „have“ düzensiz: has.

examples.de: He works in a shop.
She watches TV in the evening.
My brother has a dog.

explanation.heading: Soru ve olumsuz: do / does
explanation.tr: Soruda ve olumsuzda yardımcı fiil do/does gelir ve -s yardımcıya geçer: Does she work? — She doesn't work. Asıl fiil yalın kalır, -s almaz.

examples.de: Do you like tea?
Does he speak English?
We don't eat fish.

questions.text: She ___ in Izmir.
questions.explain: „she“ üçüncü tekil: live → lives. „is live“ diye bir biçim yok.

questions.text: ___ you like coffee?
questions.explain: „you“ ile yardımcı fiil „do“; „does“ yalnız he/she/it ile.

questions.text: He ___ tennis on Saturday.
questions.explain: „he“ ile -s: plays. Rutin için -ing biçimi kullanılmaz.

questions.text: My mother ___ (work) at a school.
questions.explain: „my mother“ = she → works.

questions.text: ___ your brother speak English? (do / does)
questions.explain: „your brother“ = he → Does. Asıl fiil yalın: speak.

questions.text: They ___ (not / drink) tea.
questions.explain: Olumsuz: do + not + yalın fiil → don't drink.

questions.text: Soruyu doğru sıraya diz.
questions.explain: Soruda sıra: Does + özne + yalın fiil: Does she live here?

questions.text: „He don't like pizza.“ — Bu cümle doğru mu?
questions.explain: „he“ ile olumsuz „doesn't“: He doesn't like pizza.

questions.text: „We go to school by bus.“ — Bu cümle doğru mu?
questions.explain: „we“ ile fiil yalın kalır: go. Cümle doğru.

questions.text: Ali ___ TV in the evening.
questions.explain: Sonu -ch ile biten fiil üçüncü tekilde -es alır: watches.

title: My First Month at the Shelter
intro: Hayvan barınağında gönüllü olan birinin ilk ayını anlattığı blog yazısını okuyacaksın.
text:
MY FIRST MONTH AT THE SHELTER

Four weeks ago I started as a volunteer at the animal shelter near my flat. I go there every Saturday morning for three hours.

On my first day I was nervous. Marta, who has worked there for nine years, showed me everything: where the food is, how much water each bowl needs, and which dogs you can walk alone.

The work is not romantic. I clean cages, I wash blankets and I carry heavy bags. But then there is the other part. Two weeks ago I walked a small brown dog called Rocky. He was scared of everything - cars, bikes, even plastic bags. Last Saturday a bus stopped next to us and he did not run away. That felt better than any thank-you.

Two dogs found a new owner last month. One of them was Rocky's friend, so now Rocky is alone again. I know this is good news, but I was sad for a day.

If you have three free hours a week, go and ask them. They always need people.

questions.text: What is the text about?
options: The writer's first weeks as a volunteer.
How to choose a dog for your family.
A shelter that will close next month.
questions.explain: Başlık ve ilk cümle bunu söylüyor: dört hafta önce gönüllü olarak başladı. Kapanma ya da köpek seçme hiç geçmiyor.

questions.text: Who is Marta?
options: The writer's neighbor who has two dogs.
A woman who has worked at the shelter for nine years.
A visitor who wants to take Rocky home.
questions.explain: „Marta, who has worked there for nine years, showed me everything.“ — deneyimli çalışan, komşu ya da ziyaretçi değil.

questions.text: The writer thinks the work is easy and beautiful.
questions.explain: „The work is not romantic. I clean cages, I wash blankets and I carry heavy bags.“ — iş ağır, güzel olan başka bir şey.

questions.text: The writer goes to the shelter every ___ morning.
questions.explain: „I go there every Saturday morning and stay for three hours.“

questions.text: Why was the bus important for the writer?
options: It showed that Rocky is less scared now.
It showed that Rocky wants a new owner.
It showed that the streets are dangerous.
questions.explain: Rocky her şeyden korkuyordu; otobüs durduğunda kaçmadı. Yazar bunu „better than any thank-you“ diye anlatıyor.

questions.text: Why was the writer sad for a day?
questions.explain: İki köpek sahip buldu; biri Rocky'nin arkadaşıydı, „so now Rocky is alone again“.

title: Joining the Sunday Ride
intro: Nadir bir bisiklet kulübünü arıyor. Hangi grup, nerede, saat kaçta ve yanında ne getirmeli - dinleyip yakala.

segments.speaker: Nadir
segments.text: Hello, is that the Riverside Cycling Club?

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Yes, Priya speaking. How can I help you?

segments.speaker: Nadir
segments.text: I saw your poster at the library. I would like to join the Sunday ride, but I have never cycled in a group.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: That is no problem. We have two groups. The fast one rides sixty kilometers, the slow one rides twenty-five.

segments.speaker: Nadir

segments.speaker: Priya

segments.speaker: Nadir
segments.text: And what do I need to bring?

segments.speaker: Priya

segments.speaker: Nadir
segments.text: Is the route difficult?

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: It is flat for twenty kilometers and then there is one hill. Last Sunday it rained and we stopped after an hour, but this week the weather looks good.

segments.speaker: Nadir

segments.speaker: Priya

title: One Small Change
intro: Önce iki cümle kur, sonra bir arkadaşına son zamanlarda değiştirdiğin bir alışkanlığı anlat.

tasks.tr: Geçen cumartesi ilk kez gönüllü olarak çalıştım.
tasks.answer: Last Saturday I worked as a volunteer for the first time.
alternatives: I worked as a volunteer for the first time last Saturday.
tasks.hint: Past simple düzenli fiilde -ed alır ve kişiye göre DEĞİŞMEZ: I worked, she worked. Zaman ifadesi başta ya da sonda durabilir.

tasks.tr: Otobüse binmedim çünkü hava çok güzeldi.
tasks.answer: I didn't take the bus because the weather was very nice.
alternatives: I did not take the bus because the weather was very nice.
I didn't take the bus because the weather was really nice.
tasks.hint: Olumsuzda zamanı „did“ taşır, asıl fiil YALIN kalır: didn't take, didn't took değil.

tasks.prompt: Son birkaç ayda küçük bir alışkanlığını değiştirdin (yürüyerek gitmek, erken kalkmak, daha az şey almak - sen seç). Bir arkadaşına yaz: ne yaptın, başta nasıldı, şimdi nasıl, ona da öner.

Başta nasıl olduğunu geçmiş zamanla anlat
Şimdi ne fark ettiğini söyle
Arkadaşına öner ve bir soru sor

phrases.de: About two months ago I started …

At first it was hard, because I had to get up earlier and my legs hurt for a week. Now I feel much better in the morning and I save forty euros a month. You should try it, because your office is even closer than mine. Let me know if you want to walk together on Monday. Selin

title: Three sounds of -ed
intro: Yazılışı hep aynı, sesi üç türlü: -ed kimi zaman „t“, kimi zaman „d“, yalnız t/d'den sonra „ıd“ olur.

tasks.hint: „walked“ tek hecedir: WOKT. Sonundaki -ed „t“ okunur, ayrı hece değildir.

confusions.fix: -ed'i ayrı hece yapma; „walked“ tek hecede biter: wokt.

tasks.de: We watched a film last night.
tasks.hint: „watched“ = WOÇT. Sessiz harften (ç) sonra -ed „t“ olur.
„called“ = KOLD. „l“ sesli bir harftir, bu yüzden -ed burada „d“ okunur.

confusions.fix: Sonu „d“: kold. Ayrı hece yok ama „d“ duyulmalı.

tasks.hint: „cleaned“ = KLİİND. Yine „d“, tek hece.
„wanted“ = WON-tıd, İKİ hece. Kök „t“ ile bittiği için -ed burada ayrı hece olur.

confusions.fix: „t“den sonra -ed ayrı hecedir: won-tıd. Burada hece eklemek DOĞRU.

tasks.hint: „waited“ = WEY-tıd, iki hece. „hour“ baştaki h okunmaz: AUIR.

tasks.de: He asked a very good question.
tasks.hint: „asked“ = AASKT, tek hece ve üç sessiz üst üste: s-k-t. Araya ünlü koyma.

heard: he ask a very good question

title: did and the past
intro: Geçmişi anlatmanın temel zamanı: düzenli -ed, düzensiz biçimler ve soruda ortaya çıkan „did“.
focus: Past simple: düzenli ve düzensiz fiiller, did ile soru ve olumsuz

explanation.heading: Kişiye göre değişmez
explanation.tr: Türkçede geçmiş zaman kişiye göre değişir: gittim, gittin, gitti. İngilizcede past simple herkes için AYNIDIR. Şimdiki zamandaki „-s“ derdi burada yok.

examples.de: I worked late yesterday.
She worked late, too.
examples.tr: O da geç saate kadar çalıştı.
examples.note: she ile de worked, works değil

examples.de: We arrived two hours ago.

explanation.heading: Düzensiz fiiller ezberdir
explanation.tr: En sık kullanılan fiillerin çoğu -ed almaz; ikinci biçimi ezberlenir. Kural yok, ama liste kısadır ve her gün karşına çıkar.

examples.de: I went to the market and bought bread.
She saw the message but forgot to answer.
examples.tr: Mesajı gördü ama cevap vermeyi unuttu.

examples.de: They had a long day.

explanation.heading: Soru ve olumsuzda zamanı „did“ taşır
explanation.tr: Soru ve olumsuz cümlede „did“ devreye girer ve geçmiş bilgisini o üstlenir. Bu yüzden asıl fiil YALIN hâle döner. En sık hata budur: „Did you went?“ yanlış, çünkü zaman iki kez işaretlenmiş olur.

examples.de: Did you see the film?
I didn't understand the question.
Why did she leave so early?

questions.text: Yesterday I ___ my grandmother.
questions.explain: Geçmiş için düzenli fiil -ed alır: visited. „Yesterday“ zamanı belli ediyor.

questions.text: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explain: Soruda zamanı „did“ taşır, asıl fiil yalın kalır: Did you finish …?

questions.text: She ___ to the party because she was ill.
questions.explain: Olumsuzda da fiil yalın: didn't come. „not came“ diye bir biçim yok.

questions.text: We ___ (go) to the beach last summer.
questions.explain: „go“ düzensizdir: go - went - gone. Burada ikinci biçim gerekir.

questions.text: ___ they enjoy the concert? (do / does / did)
questions.explain: Geçmiş zaman sorusu „did“ ile açılır; „enjoy“ yalın kalır.

questions.text: I ___ (buy) this jacket two years ago.
questions.explain: „buy“ düzensiz: buy - bought. „ago“ geçmiş zamanla kullanılır.

questions.text: Soruyu doğru sıraya diz.
questions.explain: Soru kelimesi, did, özne, yalın fiil: Where did you buy it?

questions.text: „He didn't wanted to come.“ - Is this sentence correct?
questions.explain: „didn't“ zaten geçmişi gösteriyor; doğrusu „He didn't want to come.“

questions.text: „They arrived at ten and left at eleven.“ - Is this sentence correct?
questions.explain: Biri düzenli (arrive - arrived), öteki düzensiz (leave - left); ikisi de doğru.

questions.text: Soruda ve olumsuzda asıl fiil neden yalın kalır?
options: Çünkü İngilizcede soru cümlesinde fiil çekilmez.
questions.explain: Zaman iki kez işaretlenmez: „did“ geçmişi üstlenince fiil yalın hâline döner.

title: Learning to Swim at Thirty-Five
intro: Yetişkin yaşta yüzme öğrenen bir kadının blog yazısını oku: neden başladı, ilk ders nasıl geçti, bugün nerede.
text:
I have never been a confident swimmer. When I was a child, my family lived far from the sea, and the school pool was closed for years. So I grew up as the person who sat on the beach and watched.

Last spring, my daughter started swimming lessons, and she asked me why I never came into the water with her. I didn't have a good answer. The next week, I decided to sign up for an adult beginners' course at the local pool.

The first lesson was hard. I was the oldest person in the group, and I couldn't even put my face in the water. Our teacher, Marta, didn't laugh. She told us that fear is normal and that most adults learn faster than they expect, because they listen.

Since then, I have been to the pool twice a week. I have already learned to breathe in the water, and last month I swam twenty-five meters without stopping. I haven't swum in the sea yet, but we have booked a holiday for August, and this time I won't be sitting on the beach.

If you have been thinking about lessons for years, my advice is simple: don't wait for the perfect moment. Book the first class. The rest will follow.

questions.text: What is the text mainly about?
options: why the writer prefers the beach to the pool
how the writer's daughter learned to swim
how the writer learned to swim as an adult

Her daughter asked a question she could not answer.
Her family booked a holiday by the sea.
questions.explain: „she asked me why I never came into the water … I didn't have a good answer.“ Öğretmenin sözü ve tatil daha sonra geliyor.

options: She expected too much from the group.
She was strict but very funny.
questions.explain: „Marta didn't laugh. She told us that fear is normal …“ — yazar öğretmenin anlayışını vurguluyor; sertlik ya da şaka yok.

questions.text: The writer has already swum in the sea.

questions.explain: „Since then, I have been to the pool twice a week.“ — dördüncü paragrafın ilk cümlesi.

questions.explain: „last month I swam twenty-five meters without stopping.“

title: Swapping Homes for the Summer
intro: Radyo sunucusu, tatillerini ev takasıyla geçiren Leyla'yla konuşuyor: sistem nasıl işliyor, başta neden endişeliydi, şimdi ne düşünüyor.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Welcome back. My guest today is Leyla, who has spent the last three summers in other people's homes and let other people stay in hers. Leyla, how does a home exchange work?

segments.speaker: Leyla
segments.text: It's simple, really. You put your flat on a website, with photos, and look for a family who wants to visit your city. You agree on dates, and then you just swap keys.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: And you don't pay anything?

segments.speaker: Leyla
segments.text: No rent, no. You pay for the flights, of course, but for a family of four, that saves a lot of money.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Weren't you worried about strangers living in your home?

segments.speaker: Leyla
segments.text: At first, yes, I have to admit. Before our first exchange, I hid all our photos and locked one room. It sounds silly now.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: So what changed?

segments.speaker: Leyla
segments.text: We came home, and the flat was cleaner than before. There was even a cake on the table. Since then, we have done it every year, and we've never had a real problem.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Never? Not one?

segments.speaker: Leyla
segments.text: Well, once a guest broke a lamp. He wrote us a long apology and left money for a new one. Honestly, my own children have broken more.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Any advice for someone who wants to try it?

segments.speaker: Leyla
segments.text: Be honest in your description. If the shower is slow, say so. Nobody wants surprises on holiday.

questions.text: What is the interview mainly about?
options: holidays in other people's homes without paying rent
renting your flat to tourists to make money
a website where families sell holiday photos
questions.explain: Leyla ev takasını anlatıyor: „you just swap keys“, „No rent, no.“ Para kazanmak ya da fotoğraf satmak yok.

questions.text: What did Leyla do before her first exchange?
options: She hid her photos and locked a room.
She paid the other family some money.
She cleaned the flat and baked a cake.
questions.explain: „Before our first exchange, I hid all our photos and locked one room.“ Pasta ve temiz ev, döndüklerinde buldukları şey.

questions.text: How does Leyla feel about the broken lamp now?
options: She thinks the guest should pay more.
It was not a big problem for her.
She is still angry with the guest.
questions.explain: „He wrote us a long apology … my own children have broken more.“ — özür ve karşılaştırma, olayı küçümsediğini gösteriyor.

questions.text: The guests pay Leyla rent for her flat.
questions.explain: „And you don't pay anything?“ — „No rent, no.“ Yalnız kendi uçak biletleri ödeniyor.

questions.text: Leyla'nın son tavsiye cümlesini duyduğun gibi yaz.
questions.explain: „Nobody wants surprises on holiday.“ — nobody olumsuz anlam taşır ama fiil olumlu ve tekil kalır: wants.

questions.text: How many summers has Leyla spent in other people's homes?
questions.explain: Sunucu tanıtıyor: „who has spent the last three summers in other people's homes“.

title: Should Ayla Get a Dog?
intro: Arkadaşın Ayla köpek almayı düşünüyor ve fikrini soruyor; önce iki cümle kur, sonra e-postasına görüşünü ve gerekçelerini yaz.

tasks.tr: Senin yerinde olsam yaza kadar beklerdim.
tasks.answer: If I were you, I would wait until summer.
alternatives: I would wait until summer if I were you.
tasks.hint: İkinci koşul: If + past simple (were), ana cümlede would + yalın fiil. Türkçedeki „olsam … -irdim“ kalıbı; koşul cümlesi başa da sona da gelebilir.

tasks.tr: İki yıldır bir köpeğim var ve bir kez bile pişman olmadım.
tasks.answer: I have had a dog for two years and I have never regretted it.
alternatives: For two years I have had a dog and I have never regretted it.
tasks.hint: Hâlâ süren durum: present perfect + for (süre). Türkçede „var“ şimdiki zaman; İngilizce geçmişi şimdiye bağlar: have had. never + üçüncü hâl: have never regretted.

tasks.prompt: Arkadaşın Ayla köpek almayı düşünüyor ve senin dürüst görüşünü istiyor. E-postasına cevap yaz: görüşünü açıkça söyle, en az iki gerekçe ver, kendi deneyiminden ya da tanıdığın birinden örnek ver ve ona bir soru sor.
tasks.stimulus: Hi! I need your honest opinion. I have been thinking about getting a dog for months. I live alone in a small flat, and I work from home three days a week. My neighbor says a dog would be too much for me, but I have wanted one since I was a child. What do you think? Should I do it, or should I wait? Write soon! Ayla
checklist: Görüşünü açıkça söyle: al, alma ya da bekle
En az iki gerekçe ver
Kendi deneyiminden ya da tanıdığın birinden örnek ver
Bir soru sor ve vedalaş

phrases.de: If I were you, I would …

tasks.sample: Hi Ayla, thanks for your message! In my opinion, you should get a dog, but not yet. I have had one for two years, and it is the best thing that has happened to me. But a dog needs a lot of time, and the first months are hard. Since I got mine, I have not slept late once! The problem is that you are away from home two days a week. If I were you, I would wait until you have found someone who can walk the dog on those days. Have you thought about a smaller dog? They are happier in a flat. Let me know what you decide! Love, Deniz

title: When Should You Leave Home?
intro: Gençlerin evden ayrılma yaşı üzerine kırk ile yetmiş beş saniyelik bir konuşma yap: görüşün ve en az iki gerekçen.

monologue.promptTr: Bazı gençler on sekizinde evden ayrılır, bazıları otuzuna kadar ailesiyle yaşar. Sence bir genç ne zaman kendi evine çıkmalı? Görüşünü söyle ve en az iki gerekçe ver.
bulletsTr: Görüşün: erken mi, geç mi, yoksa duruma göre mi?
Birinci gerekçe: para, bağımsızlık ya da aile
İkinci gerekçe ya da karşı görüşe kısa bir cevap
Kendi hayatından ya da tanıdığından bir örnek
monologue.sampleDe: In my opinion, young people should move out when they can pay for their own life, not at a fixed age. The main reason is that living alone teaches you things that nobody can teach you at home: how to cook, how to plan your money, how to solve problems on your own. For example, my cousin moved out at twenty, and after a year he was a completely different person. On the other hand, rents have become very high, and many young people just can't afford a flat. In that case, staying with your parents for a few more years is not a problem. That's why I think the right time depends on money and on the person, not on a number.
monologue.rubricHint: Görüş + en az iki gerekçe bekle; hedef kalıplardan en az üçü geçmeli. Present perfect (have become) ve koşul yapısı artı puan.

title: have done or did?
intro: İngilizcenin iki geçmiş zamanını ayırmayı öğren: ne zaman have + üçüncü hâl, ne zaman -ed; since/for, already/yet, ever/never işaretleri.
focus: Present perfect ile past simple: since/for, already/yet, ever/never

explanation.heading: İki geçmiş, tek -di
explanation.tr: Türkçede „Berlin'e gittim“ hem dün olanı hem hayatında bir kez olanı anlatır; İngilizce ikiye ayırır. Zaman belliyse ya da bittiyse past simple (yesterday, last year, in 2019). Zaman söylenmiyorsa ve sonuç şimdiyi ilgilendiriyorsa present perfect: have/has + fiilin üçüncü hâli.

examples.de: I went to Berlin last year.
I have been to Berlin twice.
She lost her keys yesterday.
She has lost her keys, so she cannot get in.
examples.tr: Anahtarlarını kaybetti, o yüzden içeri giremiyor.

explanation.heading: since / for: hâlâ süren durum
explanation.tr: Türkçede „beş yıldır burada yaşıyorum“ şimdiki zamandır; İngilizce bunu present perfect ile söyler, çünkü durum geçmişte başladı ve sürüyor. for + süre (for five years), since + başlangıç noktası (since 2021, since Monday). Aynı „for“ past simple ile gelirse durum bitmiştir.

examples.de: We have lived here for five years.
We have lived here since 2021.
We lived there for five years.

explanation.heading: already / yet / ever / never
explanation.tr: already olumlu cümlede have ile fiilin arasına girer („çoktan“). yet olumsuz cümlede ve soruda en sona gelir („henüz“). ever soruda „hiç“ demektir; never olumsuz cümlenin kendisidir, „hiç … -medi“ anlamını verir ve not ile birlikte kullanılmaz.

examples.de: I have already finished the report.
Have you finished yet?
Have you ever eaten Turkish breakfast?
I have never seen snow.

explanation.heading: En sık hata
explanation.tr: „I have seen him yesterday“ yanlış: yesterday zamanı sabitler ve past simple ister. „since three years“ da yanlış: since yalnız başlangıç noktası alır; süre için for.

examples.de: I saw him yesterday.
I have known her for three years.

questions.text: We ___ in Ankara for two years, then we moved to Izmir.
questions.explain: „then we moved“ — Ankara dönemi bitti. for + süre olsa da bitmiş durum past simple ister: lived.

questions.text: She ___ in this flat since 2020.
questions.explain: since + başlangıç noktası, durum sürüyor → present perfect: has lived. Türkçedeki „yaşıyor“ seni „lives“e çekmesin.

questions.text: ___ you ever been to Japan?
questions.explain: ever + been: „hayatında hiç“ sorusu → present perfect soru: Have you ever been …?

questions.text: We have known each other ___ ten years. (since / for)
questions.explain: „ten years“ bir süre → for. since yalnız başlangıç noktasıyla kullanılır (since 2015).

questions.text: I haven't seen that movie ___. (already / yet)
questions.explain: Olumsuz cümlede „henüz“ = yet, cümle sonunda. already yalnız olumlu cümlede.

questions.text: They ___ (move) to Izmir in 2018.
questions.explain: „in 2018“ zamanı sabitliyor → past simple: moved.

questions.text: He ___ (never / eat) fish.
questions.explain: Hayatında hiç: has + never + fiilin üçüncü hâli (eaten). not eklenmez.

questions.text: Soruyu doğru sıraya diz.
questions.explain: Soru sırası: Have + özne + üçüncü hâl + nesne; yet en sona: Have you finished your homework yet?

questions.text: „I have seen him yesterday.“ — Bu cümle doğru mu?

title: The five-star problem
intro: Puanlama sistemlerinin neden işe yaramaz hale geldiğini anlatan bir yorum yazısı: sorun yıldızlarda mı, bizde mi?
text:
THE FIVE-STAR PROBLEM

Somewhere between the taxi app and the food delivery, five stars stopped meaning „excellent“ and started meaning „nothing went wrong.“ Ask any driver: a four-star rating is not praise. In many companies it is a warning, and below 4.6 the account may be closed. The scale runs from one to five, but in practice it has two positions.

This happens because we are not rating a service; we are deciding whether to punish a person. Most customers know that a low score can cost someone their work, so they give five stars to anyone who was not rude. The result is an average that looks precise and tells you almost nothing. If everything is 4.8, the number is decoration.

The second problem is who writes at all. People rarely stop to praise an ordinary experience. They write when they are angry, and sometimes when a company has asked them three times. So the ratings we read come mostly from two groups: the furious and the reminded. Neither is a good sample.

Companies know this, and some of them have quietly moved the threshold. One hotel chain now treats anything below nine out of ten as a complaint. Staff are trained to ask for a ten, which is why you are handed a card explaining that „anything less than ten means we have failed.“ That sentence is not information. It is pressure, and it turns the guest into an employee of the marketing department.

None of this means feedback is useless. Written comments still work, because they cannot be averaged. A single sentence — „the room was clean but we could hear every door“ — carries more than three hundred identical stars. The problem is not that people are dishonest. It is that we asked them a question with only one acceptable answer, and then treated the answer as data.

Subject: Course B2.2 - three changes of teacher

tasks.sample:
Dear Ms. Demirci,

Thank you for taking the time to write, and I am sorry that you had to. You are right that three teachers in eleven weeks is too many, and you are also right that the repeated unit is the real issue, not the staffing.

What happened was that your original teacher left at short notice in week four and her replacement was ill in week nine. We should have sent you the course plan when the first change was made; if we had done that, the second teacher would not have started the same unit again. That was our mistake, not yours.

As a first step, we would like to credit four sessions to your account, which you can use in any course this year, or we can refund 160 euros directly. We will also send the full plan for the remaining weeks tomorrow, with the name of the teacher for each date. If neither option works for you, please call me and we will find something that does.

title: Tips or better pay?
intro: Bir buçuk dakikaya kadar konuşacaksın: iki tarafı da tart, sonra kendi konumunu koşuluyla söyle.

monologue.promptTr: Bazı ülkelerde bahşiş maaşın bir parçası, bazılarında hiç yok. Bahşiş sistemi kalmalı mı, yoksa ücretler yükseltilip kaldırılmalı mı? İki tarafı da anlat ve kendi konumunu söyle.
bulletsTr: Bahşişi savunan en güçlü argümanı anlat

targets.de: There are two ways of looking at this.
The argument in favor is that …
I would support it only if …

monologue.sampleDe: There are two ways of looking at this. The argument in favor of tipping is that it rewards the person in front of you, not the company. In a good week a waiter can earn far more than a fixed wage would ever give them, and customers feel they have some control over the service they get. The problem with that is how unequal it becomes. Research keeps showing that tips depend on things that have nothing to do with the work: the weather, the time of day, and, uncomfortably, what the server looks like. If your income depends on being liked, you cannot afford to correct a rude customer, and that changes the job itself. There is also the quiet part: tipping lets the employer move a business cost onto the guest. So I would support keeping tips only if they were genuinely extra, on top of a wage people could actually live on. If a restaurant cannot pay that wage, the answer is not a jar by the till; the answer is a higher price on the menu, printed honestly.

title: The bench with the armrest
intro: Kamusal alandaki küçük tasarım kararlarını okuyan bir deneme: bir bankın kolçağı gerçekte kime ne söylüyor?
text:
THE BENCH WITH THE ARMREST

Look at the benches in any renovated station and you will notice a detail that was not there thirty years ago: a metal armrest in the middle, sometimes two. Ask the operator why, and the answer is comfortable and almost certainly rehearsed. The armrests, you will be told, help older passengers to stand up.

That is not a lie. Some people do use them exactly that way. It is simply not the reason the bench was redesigned, and everyone involved knows it. The armrest is there so that nobody can lie down.

What interests me is not the decision itself, which at least has a logic, but the language around it. Rarely does a city announce that it intends to move homeless people out of a station; what it announces is „improved seating.“ The design does the work, and the vocabulary removes the fingerprints. Nobody has to defend a policy that was never written down, because a bench is not a policy. It is furniture.

This is what makes the practice so difficult to argue with. A rule can be challenged, published, voted on, reversed. A shape cannot. If the sloped surface makes sitting uncomfortable after ten minutes, whom exactly do you write to? Every individual object has a plausible explanation - drainage, maintenance, the flow of passengers - and it is only when you see forty of them together that the pattern becomes an argument.

I should be careful here, because the opposite position is not absurd. Stations are not shelters, and staff who are told to manage a waiting hall at two in the morning are not the villains of this story; they have been handed a social problem in the form of a cleaning schedule. What I object to is not that a choice was made. It is that the choice was made silently, and then furnished.

So the test I would apply is simple, and it is a test of language rather than of metal. If the reason a thing was built cannot be stated in one plain sentence on a sign next to it, the design is probably doing something its designers would rather not say out loud.

title: The sound of a quiet car
intro: Bir ses tasarımcısıyla söyleşi: elektrikli araçlara neden ses ekleniyor ve o sesi kim seçiyor?

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Your job title is sound designer, but you do not work in film. You design the noise that electric cars make. Where does that even begin?

segments.speaker: Ito
segments.text: It begins with a regulation. Below about twenty kilometers an hour, electric vehicles are legally required to emit a sound, because otherwise pedestrians simply do not hear them coming.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: So the brief is safety. Then why does every manufacturer sound different?

segments.speaker: Ito
segments.text: Because the regulation says how loud and roughly what frequency range, not what it should feel like. Everything above that floor is a choice, and choices get made by marketing departments as much as by engineers.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: You say that as though it troubles you.

segments.speaker: Ito
segments.text: It does, a little. There is a real tension. The safest sound is the one people already associate with danger. The most attractive sound is the one nobody has heard before.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: And you cannot have both.

segments.speaker: Ito
segments.text: Rarely. What we test for is whether a listener can tell, with their back turned, that the car is approaching and roughly how fast. Not whether they like it. Liking comes later, and honestly it comes from repetition.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Do you ever design something and then decide against it?

segments.speaker: Ito
segments.text: Constantly. We had a beautiful sound, a kind of soft rising tone, and it tested well in the studio. On a street with traffic it disappeared completely. Beautiful and useless.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Is there a sound you would refuse to make?

segments.speaker: Ito
segments.text: Anything that pretends to be an engine. Not for reasons of taste. If we teach a generation that quiet means dangerous and loud means safe, we will have solved this decade's problem and created the next one.

title: A letter to the editor

tasks.prompt: Aşağıdaki alıntıya bir okur mektubuyla cevap ver. Yazarın haklı olduğu yeri kabul et, asıl itirazını iki gerekçeyle kur, kendi ölçütünü koy ve dergiye uygun bir kayıtta yaz.
tasks.stimulus:
From „The apology economy“, this month's issue:

„Companies have finally learned to apologize. Where a decade ago a corporate statement was a wall of legal language, today it is human, specific and fast. Whatever else the last ten years have taught us, they have taught organizations to say sorry properly - and that is progress worth naming.“
checklist: Yazarın haklı olduğu noktayı kabul et
İtirazını en az iki gerekçeyle kur
Kendi ölçütünü somut biçimde koy
Dergi kaydına uygun, ölçülü bir kapanış yaz

phrases.de: What the piece does not address is …
A better test would be whether …
phrases.tr: Daha iyi bir ölçüt … olup olmadığı olurdu

phrases.de: None of this is an argument for …
phrases.tr: Bunların hiçbiri … için bir gerekçe değil

tasks.sample:
Sir,

Your correspondent is right that corporate statements have changed. The wall of legal language has gone, and what replaced it is quicker, plainer and easier to read. On the surface, that is progress.

What the piece does not address is what the new form is for. An apology that arrives within four hours and names the affected customers is not necessarily more honest than the old one; it is better rehearsed. Two things follow. First, speed has become a substitute for inquiry: an organization that apologizes on the first day cannot yet know what happened, and the sentence it publishes will quietly shape every later account of it. Second, the fluency itself is now a service that can be bought, which means the companies with the most practice at causing harm are also the ones with the best apologies.

It is precisely because these statements are so well made that they should be read as documents rather than as feelings. A better test would be whether anything in the text can be checked six months later: a named change, a date, a person who remains answerable. Warmth costs nothing; a commitment costs something.

None of this is an argument for the return of the legal wall. It is an argument for reading the new language with the same suspicion we once reserved for the old one.

Yours faithfully,
D. Karaca

Ölçtüğün şeyin ne olduğunu somut bir örnekle göster

targets.de: Let me start with what I would concede.
The strongest case for it is …
I would draw the line at …

monologue.sampleDe:
Let me start with what I would concede. The strongest case for monitoring software is not control but fairness: in a distributed team, managers who cannot see anyone tend to reward whoever is loudest in meetings, and a record of actual work can protect the quiet, competent person who would otherwise be overlooked. I have seen that argument made in good faith, and I do not think it is dishonest.

What that misses, however, is what these tools can actually measure. They count keystrokes, active windows and idle minutes, none of which is work. The most valuable half hour in my week is usually spent staring at a problem before writing a single line, and any system that scores me would record that as absence. Measure the wrong thing precisely enough and people will optimize for it - not because they are cynical, but because they would like to keep their jobs.

So I would draw the line at the level of the individual. Aggregate patterns across a department, published openly and used to change workload, seem defensible to me. A dashboard showing one person's minute-by-minute activity to their manager does not, and I would want that principle written into the contract rather than left to the goodwill of whoever happens to be in charge.

title: not only, but where the stress goes
intro: Cümlenin neyi öne çıkardığını belirleyen yapılar: devrik başlangıçlar ve vurgu cümleleri.
focus: Inversion (Not only…, Hardly…) ve cleft cümleler (It was … that / What … is)

explanation.heading: Olumsuz bir öğe başa gelirse özne geri çekilir
explanation.tr: Türkçede vurgu sözcüğü yüklemin önüne çekerek yapılır. İngilizcede sıra sabit olduğu için başka bir yol gerekir: olumsuz ya da sınırlayıcı bir öğe cümle başına alınırsa, yardımcı fiil özneden ÖNCE gelir. Bu yapı resmîdir ve az kullanıldığında güçlüdür.

examples.de: Not only did the report arrive late, it was incomplete.
examples.tr: Rapor yalnız geç gelmedi, eksikti de.

examples.de: Rarely does a city announce such a decision.
examples.tr: Bir şehir böyle bir kararı nadiren duyurur.

examples.de: Hardly had we started when the system crashed.

explanation.heading: Cleft: cümleyi ikiye bölerek vurgulamak
explanation.tr: Bir öğeyi öne çıkarmak için cümle ikiye bölünür. „It is/was X that …“ özneyi, nesneyi ya da zamanı; „What … is …“ bütün bir eylemi ya da düşünceyi vurgular. Sonuç aynı bilgidir, ama okurun dikkati başka yere düşer.

examples.de: It was the wording that troubled me, not the decision.
examples.tr: Beni rahatsız eden ifadeydi, karar değil.

examples.de: What we test for is whether the sound is audible.
examples.tr: Bizim sınadığımız şey sesin duyulup duyulmadığı.

examples.de: What the piece does not address is the purpose.

explanation.heading: Ne zaman kullanılmaz
explanation.tr: Devrik yapı her cümlede kullanılırsa metin yapmacık olur; bir paragrafta bir kez yeter. Ayrıca soru değildir: sonuna soru işareti konmaz ve „do“ yalnız yardımcı fiil yoksa eklenir.

examples.de: Never have I seen a clearer example.
Only later did we understand the reason.

questions.text: Not only ___ the deadline, but he also ignored two reminders.
questions.explain: „Not only“ başa gelince devrik yapı zorunlu: yardımcı fiil özneden önce gelir (did he miss).

questions.text: Which sentence is correctly inverted?
options: Rarely we do receive such detailed feedback.
Rarely do we receive such detailed feedback.
Rarely receive we such detailed feedback.
questions.explain: Sıra: sınırlayıcı öğe + yardımcı fiil + özne + yalın fiil.

questions.text: „It was the silence that surprised everyone.“ - What does this structure do?
options: It makes the sentence less formal.
It turns the sentence into a question.
It puts the emphasis on the silence.
questions.explain: Cleft cümlesi vurguyu „the silence“ öğesine taşır; bilgi aynı kalır, dikkat değişir.

questions.text: Rewrite with emphasis: „The wording troubled me, not the decision.“ → „It ___ the wording that troubled me.“
questions.explain: „It was X that …“ kalıbı: geçmiş için „was“, şimdiki için „is“.

questions.text: Rewrite: „We only understood the reason later.“ → „Only later ___ ___ understand the reason.“
questions.explain: „Only later“ başa gelince devrik yapı: did + özne + yalın fiil.

questions.text: Complete the cleft: „___ bothers me is the way it was announced.“
questions.explain: „What … is …“ yapısı bütün bir düşünceyi vurgular ve resmî yazıda çok kullanılır.

questions.text: Cümleyi doğru sıraya diz.
questions.explain: Olumsuz zarf, yardımcı fiil, özne, ortaç: Never have I seen such a case.

questions.text: „Not only he was late, but he forgot the files.“ - Is this sentence correct?
questions.explain: Devrik yapı eksik: „Not only was he late, but he also forgot the files.“

questions.text: „What surprised the committee was the tone of the letter.“ - Is this sentence correct?
questions.explain: Doğru bir cleft: „What …“ öbeği özne, „was“ yüklem, vurgu „the tone“ üzerinde.

questions.text: Why should inversion be used sparingly?
options: Because it is only correct in spoken English.
Because it changes the meaning of the sentence completely.
Because it draws attention to itself and sounds artificial if repeated.
questions.explain: Yapı vurgu için var; her cümlede tekrarlanırsa vurgu kaybolur ve metin yapmacık okunur.
